title: Why Your Fingers Go Wrinkly in Water

sections.name: Why Your Fingers Go Wrinkly in Water
lines: Stay in the bath long enough, and your fingers turn into prunes.
You'd think they soak up water and swell. But it's actually your nerves doing it.
After about five minutes in water, nerves tell the blood vessels in your fingertips to shrink.
The skin on top sinks down into wrinkles.
The proof? People with damaged finger nerves don't get wrinkly fingers at all.
One idea is they're for grip, like the tread on a tyre, draining water away.
In one study, people with wrinkly fingers moved wet marbles faster.
